item.title: Sharp Logarithmic Bounds for Vilenkin-Fej\'er Kernels
item.description: arXiv:2611.09929v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $G_m$ be a bounded Vilenkin group and put $R:=\sup_j m_j$. We prove the sharp uniform estimate $$\|K_n\|_1\leq \frac{17}{15\ln 2}\ln R,\qquad n\geq1,$$ for the Fej\'er kernels associated with the Vilenkin system. The constant $17/(15\ln2)$ is best possible. In the Walsh--Paley case $R=2$, the result reduces exactly to Toledo's sharp estimate $\sup_n\|K_n\|_1=17/15$.
item.dc:creator: Nika Areshidze, George Tephnadze

item.title: Graded-Edge Rakotch Contractions in Generalized Metric Spaces with Weighted Graphs
item.description: arXiv:2611.09996v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce the notion of graded-edge Rakotch contraction mappings on a generalized metric space with a weighted graph. We prove that the successive iterate of every starting point converge uniformly to a common limit, which is the unique fixed point. We derive an explicit iteration-complexity bound and, under a relaxed triangle inequality, a geometric rate whose constant is the graph invariant. Finally, we illustrate the theory on an explicit real graded contraction that realizes the interior optimum, on a quadratic integral equation, and on finite weighted digraphs.
item.dc:creator: Ismat Beg, Muhammad Aslam Javed

item.title: Excluding 54 of the 76 Nontrivial Factorization Patterns of the Cuboid Polynomial $P_{a,b,u}(t)$
item.description: arXiv:2611.10012v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $P_{a,b,u}(t)$ be Sharipov's even monic degree-$12$ third cuboid polynomial, with positive pairwise distinct rational parameters. We prove a uniform normal form for its complete factorization over $\mathbb{Q}$. Every factorization consists of at most two even quadratic factors, even irreducible factors of higher degree, and pairs of irreducible factors exchanged by $t\mapsto-t$. After dividing all degrees by the contribution of this symmetry, the normal form satisfies one degree equation, one sign equation, and an obligatory-factor alternative: an even irreducible factor of degree at least six, or an even irreducible quartic with positive rational-square constant term. The arithmetic input is a uniform construction over $\mathbb{Q}_2$, using Newton polygons, Hensel lifting, and a norm obstruction from $\mathbb{Q}_2(i)$. Valuations at all finite primes constrain rational factor constants to signed squares, while the real root equation gives exactly two simple negative roots of the auxiliary sextic. The normal form leaves exactly $22$ of the $76$ nontrivial partitions of $12$, thereby excluding $54$ complete irreducible degree patterns by one argument. Of these exclusions, $37$ follow from evenness alone and $17$ from the additional arithmetic restrictions. All local cases are proved explicitly, and an exact verification script accompanies the algebraic identities and exhaustive partition enumeration. The remaining patterns are necessary possibilities; their realization is not asserted, and full irreducibility remains open.
item.dc:creator: Valery Asiryan

item.title: Nonconstant Congruence Speeds of Integer Tetration in Non-Squarefree Radices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10018v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We further develop the theory of congruence speed for integer tetration in non-squarefree numeral systems, building on Appendix B of [M. Rip\`a and G. Di Pietro (2026), A compact notation for peculiar properties characterizing integer tetration, Notes on Number Theory and Discrete Mathematics, 32(3), 477-496]. For bases coprime to the radix, we establish an eventual floor-difference representation and determine the exact spectrum of attainable least periods. We construct explicit arithmetic progressions containing infinitely many prime bases with nonconstant congruence speed for every non-squarefree radix, thereby proving the coprime-infinitude conjecture posed in Appendix B. We also derive a uniform quadratic bound for the least coprime base with nonconstant congruence speed and establish exact natural densities of nonstabilizing bases, both among integers coprime to the radix and among those not divisible by its radical, together with the corresponding relative density among primes. Finally, we give necessary and sufficient conditions for the perfect-power congruence-speed identity (Equation (2.12) of the cited paper) to hold in arbitrary radices, determine the exact least eventual period when stabilization fails, and establish a separate criterion for the boundary case of the original parameter restriction.
item.dc:creator: Marco Rip\`a

item.title: Constructive algebraic methods for bisymmetric means
item.description: arXiv:2611.10021v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove continuity for reflexive, bisymmetric binary operations that are strictly increasing in each variable, under certain algebraic conditions. In fact, for some algebraic weights we construct a weighted quasi-arithmetic representation of such functions without assuming continuity. An elementary construction gives the case $r=2/3$. More generally, a word equality whose polynomial difference has a unique simple zero $r\in(0,1)$ forces the representation with weight $r$; every algebraic $r$ with no other conjugate in $(0,1)$ arises this way. The proof uses an affine embedding and a dense-domain extension argument.
item.dc:creator: P\'al Burai, Gergely Kiss, Patricia Szokol

item.title: Prime supports and vanishing in restricted coprime representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.10059v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the prime supports that eliminate every representation of an even integer $N$ by two positive integers coprime to $6P$. Let $J(k)$ be the largest vanishing instance obtainable with at most $k$ factors of $P$ not dividing $N/2$. We prove $k(\log k)^2\ll J(k)\ll_\varepsilon k^{4+\varepsilon}$ for every $\varepsilon>0$. The upper bound follows by comparing a classical family of shifted-prime representations with a two-dimensional upper sieve for the loss at each additional factor. Retaining the same local density factor in both estimates yields a weighted survival criterion and positivity whenever the number of noncolliding factors above $N^\theta$ is sufficiently small compared with $N^\theta$, for fixed $0<\theta<1/4$. An exact reduction separates a minimum prime cover into forced prime-pair contributions and a residual problem, and gives the lower bound for $J$ along powers of two. Residue occupancies characterize the extremal concentration at a first zero. Explicit discrepancy estimates show that supports with at most eleven factors cannot eliminate every representation when $N>2780460$, nor supports with at most seven noncolliding factors when $N\ge2266292$. Positivity for the complete support of primes up to $\sqrt N$ remains open.
item.dc:creator: Andres M. Salazar

item.title: Double sums involving quotients of binomial coefficients
item.description: arXiv:2611.10072v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is the third part of our detailed investigation of double sums where the inner sum is binomial but incomplete. We prove many identities for these double sums involving quotients of binomial coefficients and additional parameters. In addition, we evaluate some quadratic incomplete sums using Legendre polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Kunle Adegoke, Robert Frontczak, Karol Gryszka

item.title: Calculation and Recurrence Relations of the Determinants of the Hessenberg - Toeplitz Matrices
item.description: arXiv:2611.10291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The determinant D(n) of a n x n Hessenberg - Toeplitz matrix is given as product of certain functions of its elements. A compact expression of D(n) is presented and recurrence relations involving determinants and matrix elements of the Hessenberg -Toeplitz matrices are found.
item.dc:creator: Efthymios Kyriakopoulos

item.title: A Prey-Predator Framework for Tumor-Immune Dynamics: Circuit-Based Modeling with Hilfer-Katugampola Fractional Derivatives
item.description: arXiv:2611.10727v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study focuses on modeling tumor--immune interactions through a fractional-order prey--predator framework, where tumor cells act as prey and immune effector cells as predators. To capture the hereditary and memory effects inherent in biological systems, we employ the Hilfer--Katugampola fractional derivative, which flexibly interpolates between Riemann--Liouville and Caputo formulations. In addition, a circuit-based analogy is introduced to map tumor proliferation, immune regulation, and therapeutic interventions onto resistive, capacitive, and inductive elements, providing intuitive interpretation of the dynamics. Analytical investigations, including equilibrium analysis and stability criteria, are conducted across varying fractional orders. Numerical simulations reveal that lower fractional orders lead to delayed oscillations, prolonged tumor persistence, and increased sensitivity to treatment strategies compared with classical integer-order models. The integration of fractional calculus with circuit analogies offers novel insights into tumor--immune dynamics and supports the design of memory-aware therapeutic interventions.
item.dc:creator: Samaira Naz, Aamir Nadim

item.title: Monotonicity of Wang's recursive sequence and logarithmically complete monotonicity of the reciprocal of the inverse tangent
item.description: arXiv:2611.11194v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study a sequence $b_n$, posed by Fei Wang, which is defined by $b_1=\frac13$ and a convolution-type recursive relation. We derive the generating functions of $nb_n$ and of $b_n$, the latter of which is $\ln\frac{\operatorname{arctanh}x}{x}$, and represent $b_n$ as a moment integral over $[0,1]$ with a positive density. From this representation we prove that the sequence $b_n$ is positive and logarithmically convex, that the sequence $nb_n$ is strictly decreasing, and that the ratio $\frac{b_{n+1}}{b_n}$ is strictly increasing in $n\in\mathbb{N}$ with limit $1$, which answers Wang's problem. We also give a determinantal expression and closed-form formulas for $b_n$ involving Stirling numbers of the first kind and partial Bell polynomials. Finally, we prove that the function $\frac1{\arctan x}$ is logarithmically completely monotonic on $(0,\infty)$.
item.dc:creator: Feng Qi

item.title: Approximation by subsequences of matrix transform means of Vilenkin--Fourier series
item.description: arXiv:2611.11329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the rate of approximation by matrix transform means of a special subsequence of partial sums of Vilenkin--Fourier series in the spaces $L_p(G_m)$ $(1\le p<\infty)$ and $C(G_m)$.
item.dc:creator: Istv\'an Blahota, \'Akos Gy\H{o}ry

item.title: A note on two functional inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.11403v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by some recent works on the following composite functional equation: $$f(x^2+yf(z)) = xf(x)+zf(y), \quad x, y, z \in \R,$$ we solve two related functional inequalities. In each case the solutions are only the constant zero function and the identity on $\R$.
item.dc:creator: W{\l}odzimierz Fechner

item.title: The Structure of a Non-Isometric Non-Contractive Bijection of a Hereditarily Precompact Quasi-Metric Space
item.description: arXiv:2611.03681v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: On a hereditarily precompact quasi-metric space, every non-contractive bijection $F$ is asymptotically an isometry along its backward orbits: for all $a$ and $\varepsilon>0$, $0\le d(Fx,Fy)-d(x,y)<\varepsilon$ for $x$ far in the past of $a$ and all $y$. Zavarzina asked whether every such bijection of a precompact space is an isometry; the author's toll spiral (arXiv:2610.13973) answered no. Each such $F$ has a register, a quasi-pseudo-metric $\lambda^-\le d$ for which $F$ is an isometry, with round-trip distances totally bounded on orbits; after completion, $F$ acts on each orbit as a rotation of a compact monothetic group, its rigid shadow. The defect $d-\lambda^-$ from $x$ to $y$ is at most the fee of $x$ (the supremum of its defects to earlier iterates) and at least the excess of $x$'s fee over $y$'s now or at any earlier time, less their round-trip register distance; the fee never decreases forward along orbits and tends to zero backward. In this sense, every such $F$ is a toll over its rigid shadow. The fees bound the defect but do not determine it: three spirals show it can depend on $y$, vanish at a distant $y$ even when $x$ has a positive fee, and be positive toward later iterates of $x$. The toll-spiral paper asked whether every such map is conjugate to a tolled extension, a fixed toll zone over an isometric shadow, possibly with infinitely many zones. If only descents are charged, the answer is no, even up to bi-Lipschitz conjugacy; on each infinite orbit, a map is such an extension over its register exactly when its ascents carry no defect. Fees may vanish at any rate, but for zone tolls (two-valued, shift-monotone, subadditive along their routes) they reach zero at a finite depth. The general results hold on quasi-pseudo-metric spaces where every sequence has a left K-Cauchy subsequence; all but the statements listed at the end are machine-checked in Lean.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Duzer
